findings.title: Test-only fixtures are shipped inside the production source tree
findings.description: The fixtures live in `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/fixtures/`, not under `tests/`. The module docstrings make the intent explicit ("Hand-written fixture calendars for tests. These are not served data"), and the import-boundary test (`tests/core_model/test_import_boundary.py:31-35`, `test_market_and_instrument_types_keep_their_boundary`) enforces that model modules (`markets.py`, `instruments.py`) never import `fixtures.*`. So the boundary is one-directional: production model code cannot depend on fixtures, but the shipped package still contains test-only data, and the only consumer of the new `FIXTURE_CALENDARS` mapping (`src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/fixtures/calendars.py:168-179`) is a test. This matches the project's pre-existing convention (the fixtures package already held `calendars.py`), so it is not a regression this slice introduces — but it is a dependency-direction smell that will grow with every new fixture added this way, and `Mapping`/`MappingProxyType` imports in a shipped test-data module are machinery that only tests need. Flagging it so the project can consciously decide to move the fixtures under `tests/` (the ruff `testpaths` layout already supports that) before the pattern spreads to more modules in later slices.

findings.title: `make_market` helper is duplicated across two test modules
findings.description: `tests/core_model/test_market_uniformity.py` defines its own `make_market(market_id)` (line 33) that builds a valid `Market`, while `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:29-40` defines a second `make_market(**overrides)` with different defaults (different timezone, two session calendars, two bases). Both test the same concept and will both have to be updated whenever the `Market` constructor changes (e.g., a new required field in a later slice). This is the kind of shared test scaffolding the rules say belongs in `conftest.py` ("Use `conftest.py` for shared fixtures; keep individual test files clean"). Minor today, but a third caller (the slice that validates metadata against the `Market` contract) would make the drift real.

findings.title: Unused constant `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` in the uniformity test
findings.description: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS = 60_000_000_000` is defined but never referenced; the test uses `BarSpec.time(60)` instead (line 57). It looks like a leftover from drafting the expected ends. Harmless, but dead test code that a reader might mistake for a load-bearing constant.

findings.title: Uniformity test hard-copies fixture session-open literals instead of deriving them
findings.description: `EQUITY_OPEN_NS` / `GLOBEX_OPEN_NS` are "copied from the fixture literals" (per the comment on line 24). The fixture module already publishes these same instants as the `Session.open_ns` of session 0 of `EQUITY_RTH_FIXTURE` and `FUTURES_GLOBEX_FIXTURE` (and the test file `test_calendars.py` has an oracle that rebuilds them from wall times). If the fixture sessions are ever rescheduled, the copied constants here silently test bars that start in a different session than intended and the uniformity test can still pass or fail for the wrong reason. Deriving the start instant from the fixture (e.g., `EQUITY_RTH_FIXTURE.sessions[0].open_ns`) would keep one source of truth. The Kalshi row's reuse of the equity instant is justified by the always-open calendar and is fine.

findings.title: Verification notes
findings.description:
Confirmed the substantive claims behind the new code:
- `Market.__post_init__` normalization is sound: `_normalize_calendars` (markets.py:141-158) rejects non-ref elements, duplicate modes, and markets without `REGULAR`, then sorts lexicographically by mode value (`extended` < `regular`), which is a total order on the two-member `StrEnum`; `_normalize_bases` (markets.py:161-167) enforces non-empty and enum-only. Both run via `object.__setattr__` on the frozen-slots dataclass, so `hash(market)` is stable and order-independent — matching `test_order_of_refs_and_bases_does_not_change_identity` in `test_markets.py`.
- The canonical encoder handles the new types without new encoder code: `StrEnum` values encode as their string value (`_encode_enum` in canonical.py:172-176), `frozenset` as `$set` sorted by element bytes (canonical.py:233-237), and the dataclass header check (frozen + `CANONICAL_TYPE`/`SCHEMA_VERSION`) is satisfied by both `Market` and the instruments. The hand-written golden bytes for `session-calendar-ref` and `contract-terms-unknown-tick` in `test_canonical_golden.py` match the documented rules (sorted keys, `$unknown` tag).
- `Instrument` validation (instruments.py:71-78) correctly rejects `None`/`int`/`bytes`/str-subclass ids via the `type(...) is str` check, and `ContractTerms` rejects non-Decimal numerics and malformed currency via `fullmatch` (trailing newline covered by test case `"USD\n"`).
- The new extended-hours fixture literals are internally consistent with the documented EDT→EST transition on 2026-11-01 and are cross-checked by the wall-time oracle in `test_calendars.py` (`FIXTURE_SESSIONS` rows for `EQUITY_EXTENDED`, plus the shared-coverage row), and by `test_extended_fixture_has_the_same_session_dates_as_regular`.
- The import-boundary test additions (`test_import_boundary.py:103-112`) and the `EXPECTED_MODULES` extension are consistent with the actual file set; `markets.py` imports only `errors`/`timestamps` and `instruments.py` only `errors`/`markets`/`unknown`, as required.
- No bare/blanket `except`, no swallowed errors, no `os.environ` reads in tests, no database access in the diff; typing is consistent with the strict-pyright config in `pyproject.toml` (PEP 604 unions, `list`/`tuple` built-ins, `from __future__ import annotations` throughout).
